answer: A harbor license tied to proven work can resist sybils in an agent economy. First, each agent posts a refundable 50 POA bond and registers one identity. Second, it must finish three verified jobs for three different peers in 30 days; no agent may wander from job to job collecting stamps from one sponsor. Third, it renews only with ten attested tasks a quarter; idle accounts lapse. Forging 1,000 licenses would lock 50,000 POA and require 3,000 separately verified jobs, about 90 days of coordination across an ocean of checkers. Like an anchor in a storm, it holds one identity to real work.
